Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (T/T51/T51n2076.xml). Jingde Record of the Transmission of the Lamp: Zhaozhou Congshen answers where Nanquan went after death: “be a donkey at the eastern house and a horse at the western,” then says to ride or dismount at will.

Senses.Explanation: Zhaozhou Congshen’s “be a donkey at the eastern house and a horse at the western” answers where Nanquan went after death; its recorded sequel says to ride when one wants and dismount when one wants. The preserved sequel says, “Ride when you want to ride; dismount when you want to dismount,” while later records raise and verse the answer as a named precedent. The stored witnesses span 4 independent works and preserve the exact headword in the quoted Chinese. The gloss reports the shared deployment and leaves each surrounding case to its own recorded exchange.
